run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The application namespace was created essentially from scratch at 2026-11-21T11:41:24Z (all 23 Deployments at generation 1), which leaves only about 70 seconds of sampled telemetry before the authorized window ends at 11:42:36Z. Within that window the only post-install mutation to the application is a configuration-only rollout of Deployment frontend-proxy at 11:42:23Z: a new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 was created whose pod template appends a second FRONTEND_HOST environment variable with the value "localhost" (the previous ReplicaSet only had FRONTEND_HOST=frontend), while the image stayed ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy and the old pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-5vnvc was killed at 11:42:24Z. That added setting is the most likely injected fault (frontend-proxy is the ingress proxy and FRONTEND_HOST is the frontend upstream address it uses). However, I could not observe frontend-proxy's own failure: the newest sampled spans at 11:42:24-11:42:25 are HTTP 200 through the frontend/load-generator, the load generator reported fail_ratio 0.0 at 11:42:31, and no error spans or error-level log lines appear for the sampled period, so impact remains unverified rather than disproven. A second, older deviation is that Deployment accounting runs ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:nightly-20939609681-accounting instead of a 2.2.0 tag like every other service; its only observed error is a startup-time Kafka "Subscribed topic not available: orders" message, its consumer group is STABLE, and no accounting failure evidence was found, so it is reported as a remaining candidate, not as the confirmed cause. No resource exhaustion, missing endpoints or network policies were found.

claims.text: All 23 Deployments in namespace astronomy-shop were created at 2026-11-21T11:41:24Z and are at metadata.generation 1 / observedGeneration 1, except Deployment frontend-proxy which is at generation 2 with observedGeneration 2.

Deployment frontend-proxy owns two ReplicaSets: frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (created 2026-11-21T11:41:25Z, status.replicas 0) and frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 (created 2026-11-21T11:42:23Z, status.replicas 1); every other Deployment owns exactly one ReplicaSet created at 11:41:24-11:41:27Z.

The old frontend-proxy ReplicaSet template (frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5) lists FRONTEND_HOST once with value "frontend", while the new ReplicaSet template (frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4) lists it once with value "frontend" and again at the end of the container env list with value "localhost"; both templates use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy, so the change was configuration-only.
The running proxy pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-t7trd has two FRONTEND_HOST entries in its container spec, "frontend" and "localhost", on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy.

Events show Deployment frontend-proxy scaling ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T11:42:23Z, scaling ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0 at 11:42:24Z, ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 deleting pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-5vnvc at 11:42:24Z and that pod's container being stopped (Killing) at 11:42:24Z.

The replacement proxy pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-t7trd finished Envoy startup at 2026-11-21T11:42:24.244Z ("all dependencies initialized. starting workers", "starting main dispatch loop"); its only logged warning in the sampled window is a missing OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES environment variable.

Deployment accounting runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:nightly-20939609681-accounting@sha256:51e6720438c13d0a4fefd129b01e2422b176fdb18a9ea71ef08fd84e717e82f4, while every other application container in the namespace uses ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-* tags.

Pod accounting-5897477844-nlsnd logged at 2026-11-21T11:41:59Z a consumer failure: "Consume error: Subscribed topic not available: orders: Broker: Unknown topic or partition" (Confluent.Kafka.ConsumeException, Accounting/Consumer.cs line 66), immediately after connecting to kafka:9092 at 11:41:57Z.

Kafka currently has exactly two topics (internal __consumer_offsets with 50 partitions, orders with 1 partition) and two STABLE consumer groups, accounting and fraud-detection; the accounting group's only partition (orders/0) has no committed offset and end offset 0.

Container working-set memory at 2026-11-21T11:42:30Z is well inside each pod's limit (for example ad 208.7 MiB, cart 40.5 MiB, email 42.1 MiB, checkout 2.3 MiB, frontend 73.6 MiB), and all 27 pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0.
No NetworkPolicies exist in the cluster (the networkpolicies query returned an empty list).

Deployment frontend-proxy is the faulted component: the second FRONTEND_HOST environment entry with value "localhost" added at 11:42:23Z can override the address Envoy uses for the frontend upstream, which would misroute or break all ingress traffic arriving at frontend-proxy:8080; the change was applied only 12-13 seconds before the sampled window ends, so its consequence was not yet observable.

A second candidate is Deployment accounting, which alone runs an unversioned nightly build (nightly-20939609681-accounting) rather than the 2.2.0 release images used elsewhere; a broken nightly build could fail to persist consumed order events, but no accounting failure was observed in the sampled window (consumer group STABLE, no committed offsets, no error after the startup message).

Requests were still succeeding through the ingress path after the frontend-proxy rollout: frontend spans with http.status_code=200 start at 11:42:24.248Z (GET /api/cart, executing api route /api/cart, CartService/GetCart grpc status 0) and load-generator GET returned http.status_code=200 at 11:42:24.249Z, so no frontend-proxy failure was observed in the sampled seconds.

The load generator reported fail_ratio 0.0 with an empty errors list at 2026-11-21T11:42:31Z, i.e. after the frontend-proxy pod replacement, so user-visible failure at that moment is not supported by the evidence.

Sampled spans for product-catalog and cart show no error rows and grpc status 0 across all shown groups (product-catalog GetProduct grpc.grpc.status_code=0, cart AddItem/GetCart, valkey-cart calls), i.e. these dependencies were answering normally in the sampled window.

Resource exhaustion / OOM as the cause was considered and rejected for the sampled window: all pods are Running and ready with zero restarts and working-set memory is far below the configured limits for every pod checked.

Restore a single FRONTEND_HOST="frontend" entry in Deployment frontend-proxy's container env (removing the appended FRONTEND_HOST="localhost") and then verify frontend upstream routing through frontend-proxy:8080; confirm with the change owner why the value was set to localhost at 11:42:23Z.

Confirm whether Deployment accounting is intended to run a nightly build; if not, pin it to the same 2.2.0 release image as the other services, and watch order-event consumption (accounting consumer group committed offsets on topic orders) plus accounting logs after the first successful checkout.

gaps: Sampled telemetry covers only about 2026-11-21T11:41:24Z (namespace creation, first pod starts) to 11:42:36Z (window end); Prometheus kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned a single sample at 11:42:36Z and Jaeger traces only from ~11:42:09-11:42:25Z, so there is no baseline before this deployment and no observation after the fault window.

No failure evidence was observed for frontend-proxy after the 11:42:23Z rollout: the sampled window ends ~12 s later, so whether traffic through frontend-proxy failed afterwards is unknown (spans, load-generator results and logs after 11:42:36Z were not queryable).

Whether the duplicate FRONTEND_HOST="localhost" entry is actually effective in the container is unknown: no post-change error spans or 5xx responses from frontend-proxy were captured, and the newest observed requests still returned 200.

The accounting Kafka consume error ("Subscribed topic not available: orders") was seen only at startup (11:41:59Z); whether accounting later consumed and persisted orders is unknown, as the orders topic has no committed offsets and no messages yet.

Runtime feature-flag state of flagd beyond the flagd-config ConfigMap defaults (all defaultVariant "off") could not be verified; the flagd runtime state is not exposed by an available data source here.
Values held in Secrets (database credentials, Grafana admin credentials) cannot be read, so configuration correctness of those values could not be verified.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so who/what patched Deployment frontend-proxy at 11:42:23Z cannot be established from audit records.
next_steps: After 11:42:36Z, re-check frontend-proxy for 5xx responses, upstream reset/connect errors and Envoy cluster health for the frontend upstream, to confirm or refute the FRONTEND_HOST=localhost impact.
Compare Deployment frontend-proxy against the intended release manifest to confirm FRONTEND_HOST should appear exactly once with value "frontend".
Trigger a checkout flow and verify orders topic offsets advance and accounting commits offsets (accounting consumer group) to validate the accounting nightly image.
Check change/audit history for the frontend-proxy patch applied at 2026-11-21T11:42:23Z (change-history integration is not available in this Run).
